I STRONGLY URGE you to vote OUGHT NOT TO PASS on LD693, An Act to support the department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Corporations, Elections and Commissions. In essence this bill cost the Maine taxpayers almost $550,000! We are a poor state. We are an unfriendly environment for businesses due to high taxes, inhibiting regulations, aging infrastructure, outrageous energy costs, government overreach, etc.,etc. We need to put money into programs that will encourage companies to bring their businesses to Maine. Adding more taxes to Maine to pay for useless positions in government is not the best use of our tax dollars. The taxes in my town have raised my taxes almost 400% in the last 20 years. It's numbing to think we need to spend $550K to help the S.O.S. do the job. The answer for most bureaucrats to solve an issue is to just throw more money at it, instead of doing a more efficient job! I ask you to make the S.O.S. accountable for doing the job more efficiently! Vote OUGHT NOT TO PASS on LD693. Thank you from all the taxpayers of Maine!

Testimony in Favor of
L.D. 693 "An Act to Support the Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of
Corporations, Elections and Commissions"
Shenna Bellows Secretary of State, Department of the Secretary of State
March 19, 2025
Senator Baldacci, Representative Salisbury, and Members of the ]oint Standing Committee on
State and Local Government, my name is Shenna Bellows. I am the Secretary of State. I am
providing testimony in favor of L.D. 693.
Among the responsibilities of the Division of Corporations, UCC and Commissions is to serve as a
repository and filing office for all records relating to the business entities and nonprofit corporations operating in the State and liens filed on personal property. The Division also administers the appointment, renewal and continuing education of Notaries Public and Marriage Officiants; administers the application process of Dedimus Iustice candidates for the Governor's Office; records appointments to boards and commissions and publishes vacancy listings; and processes authentications, apostilles and incumbencies certifying the acts of public officials.
There are only 13 staff members in the Division, which has not had a new position added since
1993.
When I first became Secretary of State, the Division had a backlog of work, which at that time
seemed to be likely a result of the COVID-19 pandemic. Given the types of work backlogs other sectors were seeing, along with the in-migration of new folks to Maine, this seemed logical at the time. To solve it, I authorized hiring three temporary contract staff members to get us caught up.
We currently have 4 part-time temps working in the Division, and the backlogs have not gone away. A closer review of the issue after my first year on the job indicated that the number of
corporate filings across all categories had increased substantially over the last decade, dramatically increasing the workload of the Division. I have included charts at the end of this testimony so you can see the sustained and continual growth in work the Division has been
handling.
I01 State House Station, Augusta, Maine 0433 3-01 01 www.Maine.g0v/sos/cec; tel. 207-624-7736

Last year, the Division of Corporations handled over 35,500 new filings and changes to current entities, an increase of about 15,250 total filings or 75% seen by the division since 2015. While
this is welcomed news for Maine businesses and our state's economy, the serious increase has also resulted in an unprecedented high volume of work.

lt is simply not feasible for our small and very experienced team to be able to process such an
enormous increase in workload without additional human resources. The unfortunate result is sustained backlogs, more expensive filings by those who can afford it to get quicker turnarounds, and longer waits for those who can't afford it, or who don't know or think to file for same-day or
next-day completions. '
This is a burden on Maine businesses. We hear routinely from business owners and their
legislators about the length of time it takes to get formation filings turned around and the challenges it poses to starting businesses or getting projects off the ground.

L.D. 693 would convert the three temp positions into full-time Office Specialist II positions. This

would help us keep talent in the Division, as it has proven hard to keep good people on temp

contracts. These positions are vital to the Division getting its work done more efficiently, which

would be a welcome benefit to Maine's business community.

_

These positions were also proposed in the biennial budget, and the initiative was supported by a
majority of members on the Veterans and Legal Affairs Committee. We appreciate Senator Pierce
also submitting a bill to establish the positions, as we are agnostic as to how these positions are
created. The budget proposal also funded the positions from an Other Special Revenue fund,
which we remain open to using in this proposal as well.
For all these reasons, we support this bill. Thank you for your time, and I am happy to answer
any questions.

Testimony of Senate Majority Leader Teresa S. Pierce introducing
LD 693, An Act to Support the Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Corporations,
Elections and Commissions Before the Joint Standing Committee on State and Local Government
March 19, 2025

Chair Baldacci, Chair Salisbury, and esteemed members of the Joint Standing Committee on
State and Local Government, my name is Teresa S. Pierce. I serve as the Senate Majority Leader,
representing Senate District 25, which includes Falmouth, Cumberland, North Yarmouth,
Yarmouth (majority), Gray, and Long Island. I am pleased to be here today to introduce LD 693,
An Act to Support the Department of the Secretary of State, Bureau of Corporations,
Elections and Commissions.

Last summer, I heard from two constituents, Sean in North Yarmouth and Richard in Falmouth,

who shared their experience with the Department of the Secretary of State's Division of

Corporations. They both work in the private sector with local and out of state clients and noticed

that the Division was "extremely overworked and backlogged." I agree.

in

have the resources and staff capacity to do so. The Division of Corporations has not received any

new positions from the Legislature in well over a decade. Secretary of State Shemia Bellows has

worked to alleviate this backlog by bringing on temporary staff who continue their work today.

LD 693 would fund three Office Specialist II positions within the Bureau of Corporations,
Elections and Commissions. Office specialists at the Division of Corporations assist and advise many Maine residents daily through a myriad of issues and questions. They often make the difference for being certified and able to apply for business bank accounts, delivering on payroll, taking out new insurance policies and securing transactions with clients across the state and
country. Supporting businesses, especially small businesses, that cannot afford the delay in processing time is an issue I believe cuts across party lines.

I have the utmost respect for the workforce at the Department of the Secretary of State. Their
efforts truly benef1tMainers in more ways than we can imagine. LD 693 would honor their work
and be a tremendous service to Maine's business leaders, allowing them to focus on their companies and continue growing our economy.

Thank you for the opportunity to present this bill. Secretary Bellows is here to testify as well, I
am happy to answer questions but would defer specific or operational questions to the Secretary.
